description: OmniClaude Core Hooks - OMN-13244 measurement baseline with the OMN-13856, OMN-14330, OMN-15062, OMN-15213, OMN-16277, OMN-16162, OMN-16471, OMN-16478, OMN-17006, OMN-17168, OMN-17190, OMN-17207, and OMN-17020 carve-outs. Every context-injection/measurement hook stays DISABLED; the only re-registered hooks are the Done-flip durable-evidence guard (OMN-13856, operator-approved, no fake Done), the OMN-7018 worktree canonical-root guard (OMN-14330, blocks `git worktree add` outside $OMNI_HOME/omni_worktrees), the SubagentStop secret-leak guard (OMN-15062, blocks a subagent's final report from completing when it matches a known secret pattern -- narrowly scoped security control), the SubagentStop report-contract guard (OMN-15213, fails a lane RED when its final return is bare-Done-class instead of the report the golden-chain contract requires), the PostToolUse Bash-output secret-redaction guard (OMN-16277, masks secret-shaped patterns in raw Bash tool_response text via hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput before it lands in the transcript -- narrowly scoped security control, same class as OMN-15062, NOT a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks), the SessionStart/SessionEnd/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse(.*) bus-mirror hooks (OMN-16162, direct-dispatch a session-started/session-ended/prompt-submitted/tool-executed event to omnimarket's node_event_emit_effect, backgrounded and fail-open -- the local-bus-mirror transport superseding the OMN-16090 HTTP spool-shipper stopgap; S0 wired SessionStart/SessionEnd, S1 extends the identical pattern to UserPromptSubmit and a dedicated catch-all PostToolUse entry that never touches tool_response, kept separate from the OMN-16277 Bash-matcher secret-redaction guard), the OMN-16471 lane-death pair (PreToolUse on ^(Task|Agent|Workflow)$ records a durable OPEN lane record at the dispatch seam -- pure observer, always exit 0, always silent, so it can never refuse or delay a dispatch; SubagentStop classifies HOW the lane ended from transcript evidence -- tool-call count, wall duration, and the F-09 death signatures -- writes the paired terminal record, and blocks once on a zero-work death so `onex-lane-reconcile` can fail on any lane that has a dispatch record and no terminal one), and the PreToolUse SendMessage lane-liveness guard (OMN-16478, blocks a message that declares another lane dead or authorizes a takeover of its work unless an independent filesystem probe returns DEAD, and refuses a bare harness ref used as an address). None of these re-registrations is a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks. All other scripts remain on disk and re-registration stays a pure config change. Tenth carve-out: the PreToolUse overseer foreground-block guard (OMN-17006, re-registering the OMN-8376 guard that the OMN-13244 baseline unregistered -- blocks foreground Bash/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit/MultiEdit against repo paths while `$ONEX_STATE_DIR/overseer-active.flag` marks an overseer contract as driving, so the lead agent cannot drift into manual fixes; allows everything when the flag is absent). Its sibling from the same audit, the OMN-8928/8929 dispatch-claim pre/post pair, is DELIBERATELY NOT re-registered: its `exit 2` is swallowed by the error-guard EXIT trap (it never calls `trap - EXIT`), its deny payload uses a `{"type":"permissionDenied"}` shape this harness does not honour, and its claimant falls back to the shared constant `session`, so two anonymous lanes can never collide. Both scripts stay on disk, unregistered; OMN-17005 carries the four re-registration ACs and the expiry condition (unmet identity AC => close won't-fix and delete, do not carry dead code). Authority for both decisions: docs/tracking/2026-08-29-beta-off-the-rails-analysis.md, mechanism A1. STANDING RULE (OMN-17006, from that report's addendum): any future baseline-style disable of a hook registered here MUST land in the same change as an expiry condition and a named re-enable ticket recorded in this description, and that record MUST name all four of: OWNER -- the person or lane accountable for restoring it; REASON -- why this specific hook is off, not merely that it is; EXPIRY -- the absolute condition or date after which the disable is void; RESTORATION -- the automatic behaviour that re-registers the hook once the expiry is reached, and the re-enable ticket that tracks it. A disable with no expiry and no re-enable ticket is how OMN-13244 left enforcement dark for months while the rule it enforced was corrected by hand ~61 times. Eleventh carve-out: the SessionStart goal-surface hook (OMN-17168, session_start_goal_surface.sh -- prints the `state_as_of` of $KNOWLEDGE_BASE_INTERNAL_PATH/beta/GOAL.md, its age, and the goal rows, and when that goal is missing or older than 12h prints the exact re-baseline command `Workflow({ name: 'morning-ground-state', args: { date: '<today>' } })`). It is print-only: pure bash with no interpreter, no network, no writes, no state, and it exits 0 on every user-visible outcome including a missing file and an unset env var, so it can neither refuse nor delay a session. Its one non-zero path (exit 3) is an existing-but-unreadable GOAL.md, reported with full absolute paths; exit 3 does not block SessionStart. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_INTERNAL_PATH has NO default (CLAUDE.md rule 8): a guessed clone path would surface another checkout's goal as if it were this one, so an unset variable prints the variable name and the expected value instead. It is not a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks -- it injects one artifact the session is already required to open from (memory feedback_session_goal_from_ground_state_reconciled_to_plan), not model-generated context. Per the STANDING RULE above, its own carve-out record: OWNER -- Jonah Gray / the session-goal lane; REASON -- the durable session goal is invisible at session start, so it is remembered rather than read, which is the same dark-enforcement class as OMN-13244 itself; EXPIRY -- when OMN-17169 lands the goal projection (ground-state EFFECTs -> reconcile COMPUTE -> goal REDUCER -> ORCHESTRATOR) and GOAL.md stops being the source of truth; RESTORATION -- at that expiry the hook is REPOINTED from the file read to the projection read and stays registered under this same entry; it is not unregistered, and OMN-17169 carries that repoint as a closeout AC. The named workflow is the acknowledged stopgap. Twelfth and thirteenth carve-outs: the OMN-17190 workspace-reconcile pair (workspace_reconcile_tick.sh on PostToolUse(.*), and session_start_workspace_sync.sh on SessionStart). The tick keeps the canonical clones and the locally-installed venvs tracking dev automatically -- at most once every ONEX_RECONCILE_TICK_SECONDS (default 600) it fetches each canonical clone, fast-forwards the CLEAN ones on dev/main, and runs omnibase_infra/scripts/reconcile-workspace-venvs.sh, writing a receipt line per repo (old -> new SHA) and a one-line verdict. It NEVER pulls into a dirty clone -- it reports it -- and it never touches a clone parked on a feature branch. It runs its body DETACHED and exits 0 on every path, so it can neither refuse, delay, nor fail a tool call; when the throttle interval has not elapsed its whole cost is one stamp-file read. It is not a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks: it injects nothing into the model's context and emits no measurement event -- it is workspace maintenance, and its only user-visible output is the SessionStart line. That sibling hook is print-only: pure bash, no interpreter, no network, no writes, reading exactly one file (the tick's status line) and printing it with its age, labelling any verdict older than 30 minutes -- or of unknown age -- as unproven rather than rendering it as fresh. Why they exist (operator, 2026-08-30): "Why is anything hand built? ... omnimarket has a dependency file that specifies what should be installed. We need a process that either (1) disconnects the local installation from the canonical clones, or (2) automatically pulls the clones whenever a PR is merged and refreshes the venv." Option 2 was chosen, and until this pair landed the 'refresh the venv' half was a command a human had to read off a refusal and type. Per the STANDING RULE above, the carve-out record: OWNER -- Jonah Gray / the workspace-reconcile lane; REASON -- clone and venv drift was visible only as a mid-task dispatch refusal, and repairing it was hand-run, which is the dark-enforcement class this baseline's own history is made of; EXPIRY -- when OMN-17190's named node-based successor lands (a NodeCompute drift-detect handler behind a NodeEffect reconcile publisher, driven by the runtime and emitting its receipt to the bus); RESTORATION -- at that expiry the tick is REPLACED by the runtime-driven effect and the SessionStart hook is REPOINTED from the status file to the resulting projection; the SessionStart entry stays registered under this same record and is not unregistered, and OMN-17190 carries that repoint as a closeout AC. Thirteenth carve-out: the OMN-17207 LOCAL-CAPTURE pair — post_tool_use_auto_checkpoint.sh and post_tool_use_changeset_guard.sh — re-registered on a Bash matcher, LAST in PostToolUse order. Both are re-enables of hooks the OMN-13244 baseline unregistered, and both are revived as DURABLE LOCAL CAPTURE ONLY: they write to the local filesystem and emit NOTHING on stdout. auto-checkpoint writes ~/.claude/handoffs/checkpoint-<ts>.md on a `git commit` (commit sha, branch, message, diff --stat file count, active plan, PR number+state); changeset-guard appends one JSON line to ~/.claude/changeset-guard-events/events.jsonl when a commit exceeds 15 files. Three deliberate changes from the pre-OMN-13244 versions, each closing a defect the archaeology of 2026-08-30 found: (1) the `printf '%s' "$TOOL_INFO"` passthrough echo on every branch is REMOVED — plain PostToolUse stdout is debug-log-only, but echoing the payload back re-emits the raw tool_response that the OMN-16277 secret-redaction guard masks on this same Bash matcher; (2) changeset-guard's advisory context injection is NOT revived, only its JSONL side-write — per-turn injection is the token cost OMN-13244 removed, and the JSONL series was the only durable machine-readable output the entire pre-baseline hook surface ever produced (2,703 lines over 56 days); (3) auto-checkpoint's `gh pr view` is bounded by `timeout 5`, and its retention cap is raised from 5 to OMNICLAUDE_CHECKPOINT_RETENTION (default 200) — the 5-file cap is why only 5 checkpoints, all from one 8-hour window, survived to be examined. Neither hook publishes to the bus: that half stays gated behind OMN-17209, so this is not an OMN-16162-class transport re-enable. Registration order is pinned by test: these two come AFTER the secret-redaction guard, because updatedToolOutput is last-writer-wins and only a hook that emits the field can clobber it — these emit nothing. Per the STANDING RULE above, the OMN-17207 carve-out record: OWNER — Jonah Gray / the observability ladder lane (epic OMN-16176); REASON — the ledger records that a Bash ran for 265 ms but not that the tree changed, so every claim of work is unfalsifiable from the ledger; these two hooks restore the git-delta and changeset-magnitude fields locally while the bus half is designed; EXPIRY — when OMN-17207 (C11) lands work.delta events on the bus with the C10 identity block, and OMN-17209 clears the egress/redaction gate that keeps these payloads local today; RESTORATION — at that expiry these two hooks are SUPERSEDED, not merely unregistered: the checkpoint markdown and the JSONL series are replaced by work.delta events and their projection, and OMN-17207 carries that removal as a closeout AC so the local files cannot outlive the bus path and become a second, divergent authority. Hook-inventory carve-out (numbered by ticket, not by ordinal -- the ordinal chain above collides at 'thirteenth'): the SessionStart hook-inventory parity check (OMN-17020, session_start_hook_parity.sh -- reports any disagreement between plugins/onex/hooks/contracts/hook_inventory.yaml, this file, the scripts on disk, and this machine's ONEX_HOOKS_MASK). It is WARN ONLY by construction: every path in the script ends in exit 0, including its own failures, because a hook-manifest mismatch must never make the machine unusable; the fail-closed half of that control is the hook-inventory-gate CI check. Per the STANDING RULE above, its own carve-out record: OWNER -- the omniclaude hooks lane; REASON -- OMN-13244 gutted this file with no inventory of what went dark, and the enforcing hook for a rule corrected by hand ~61 times sat unregistered for months because nothing could answer the question which hooks are supposed to be on; EXPIRY -- none, this is a standing control, not a stopgap; RESTORATION -- not applicable to a registration (the four fields are required of DISABLES; this record exists so a future reader can evaluate the registration on the same terms). Background-agent model carve-out (OMN-17499, numbered by ticket): the PreToolUse background-agent model guard (pre_tool_use_agent_model_guard.sh on ^(Workflow|Agent)$ -- refuses a Workflow dispatch whose agent() calls do not each name an allowed background model, and an Agent dispatch with no allowed model or with subagent_type 'fork', which always inherits the parent's model). On 2026-09-01 one session dispatched 41 workflow scripts whose agent() calls omitted `model:`; every one inherited the parent session's model, which is banned for background work. The control in place was a memory entry, and it failed 41 times silently in a single session: 131 agent() call sites across 101 scripts, 38 of them with no explicit model by structural re-count -- a 29 percent miss rate that surfaced only in a forensics pass hours after the work had already run. Those scripts live under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/workflows/scripts/ and are in NO repository, so a pre-commit hook or a repo CI validator never sees them; the dispatch seam is the only place the omission is observable before the cost is paid, which is why this is a refusal and not a linter. It is registered AHEAD of the OMN-16471 lane_open observer on purpose, so a refused dispatch does not first write a phantom OPEN lane record. Fail-closed boundary: any tool other than Workflow/Agent, and any non-OmniNode repo, is passed through untouched; a Workflow or Agent dispatch this guard cannot evaluate (unparseable payload, missing decision core, unreadable scriptPath, unresolvable interpreter, unreadable allowlist) is BLOCKED, because a model choice that cannot be verified is refused rather than assumed. The allowlist is config -- plugins/onex/hooks/config/agent_model_allowlist.json, shipping opus/sonnet/haiku -- and carries deliberately NO 'inherit' entry: an inherited model is the defect, so there is no spelling of it that passes. The allow path emits nothing at all, because the Workflow payload carries the entire script body and re-emitting it would copy every prompt into the hook output stream. It is not a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks: it injects nothing and measures nothing, it only refuses. Per the STANDING RULE above, its own carve-out record: OWNER -- the omniclaude hooks lane; REASON -- the background model is an inherited, invisible default, so its omission is unobservable at author time and at run time alike, which is the same dark-enforcement class as OMN-13244 itself; EXPIRY -- none, this is a standing control, not a stopgap; RESTORATION -- not applicable to a registration. Gating note: it calls onex_hook_gate PRE_TOOL_AGENT_DISPATCH_GATE rather than a bit of its own, because EnumHookBit lives in omnibase_core and all 60 default-mask positions are allocated (60-62 are the disabled-by-default trio, 63 is bash's sign bit), so minting a new bit is a cross-repo release chain; that is the same constraint and the same resolution pre_tool_use_pr_ownership_guard.sh recorded for BASH_GUARD, and the borrowed bit's own script is unregistered under this baseline so nothing else is gated by it. AUTHORITY NOTE (OMN-17020): this description is no longer the only record of what is registered and what is dark. plugins/onex/hooks/contracts/hook_inventory.yaml is the typed inventory -- every registration here must be declared there with an owner, a ticket, a purpose and either an end-to-end canary or a stated reason one cannot be run, and every deliberate disable must carry the four STANDING RULE fields as typed data (owner, reason, an absolute review_by date, and a restoration naming its kind, its re-enable ticket and its action). The hook-inventory gate fails closed on any drift between the two, so a registration added here without a declaration there, or a hook quietly removed from here, is a failing check rather than something a reader has to notice.
